angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 37,846,080 km at 41067.20 pc = 0.01 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10, HV 1345: Baade-Wesselink distance (pc) 41067.2 +/- 1484.6 (Monte-Carlo) (https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.5478): 41067.2 +/- 1484.6 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax -0.0532 +/- 0.0174 mas (same row, RUWE 1.08), -3.1 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 54.4 +/- 1.9 solar radii from Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10, HV 1345: Baade-Wesselink mean radius (solar radii) 54.4 +/- 1.9 (Monte-Carlo) (https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.5478): 37,846,080 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 5375 +/- 153 K from Groenewegen & Lub (2023), A&A 676, A136, VizieR J/A+A/676/A136/table1, Name=SMC0368, columns Teffp, e_Teffp: Teff 5375 +/- 153 K from a fit to the spectral energy distribution at mean light (not spectroscopic) (https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.07559). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Groenewegen & Lub (2023), A&A 676, A136, VizieR J/A+A/676/A136/table1, Name=SMC0368, columns Teffp, e_Teffp: Teff 5375 +/- 153 K from a fit to the spectral energy distribution at mean light (not spectroscopic) (https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.07559)
limbDisplayGravitySource: no gravity of this star is published (none in SIMBAD); Luck (2018), AJ 156, 171, table 3 (the spectroscopic gravities of its Cepheid spectra) gives the class's range, log g -1.33 to 2.86. Across log g 0 to 2.85, the part the grid covers, the limb laws differ by at most 1.7% of the centre brightness from the one drawn, at log g 1.05, the gravity closest to all of them; log g 1.05 is a display choice, not a measurement (https://vizier.cds.unistra.fr/viz-bin/VizieR?-source=J/AJ/156/171/table3)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
